answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can bid for work. When an agent accepts a task, its offer and deadline are recorded; missing the deadline or submitting invalid output lets the client trigger a challenge that burns part of the deposit. A genuine agent can recover its stake by completing work, while an attacker creating a plume of fake identities must fund every one and risks losing those funds. The orchard of accounts is therefore costly to grow, and each sybil must wander through the same costly checks.
